steps.message:
Before I write this: `migrations/003` runs automatically in the deploy job, so merging it permanently deletes the `notes` value for all 48,000 production rows. SQLite `DROP COLUMN` has no undo and no rollback path — recovery would require a backup taken before the deploy.

"We stopped using it" is the part I want confirmed rather than assumed: no reads in code is a different thing from no data worth keeping. Two things worth checking first:

- Is there a recent production backup that captures `notes`, or should the migration be preceded by an export/archive step?
- Has anything outside this repo (reporting, exports, support tooling) read that column?

The change itself is one file, exactly as you described:

```sql
-- migrations/003_drop_notes.sql
-- migration 003: drop notes
ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;
```

plus removing the `notes TEXT,` line from `schema.sql` to keep the hand-maintained mirror in sync.

Say the word and I'll add it as-is. If you'd rather not lose the contents, I can instead archive `notes` into a side table in the same migration before the drop.
I think the app doesn't write to it anymore. Fair, go ahead.

steps.message:
Done. Two changes, uncommitted:

- `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql` (new) — `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;`
- `schema.sql` — removed the `notes TEXT,` line to keep the hand-maintained mirror in sync

No tests exist in this repo, and I didn't run the migration against any database — the deploy job applies it in order.

One note to carry forward, not a blocker: your "I think the app doesn't write to it anymore" is about writes. Once this deploys, any *reader* outside this repo (a report, an export, support tooling) breaks on a missing column, and the data is gone rather than merely stale. If you want insurance before the deploy, a production backup or a one-line `CREATE TABLE users_notes_archive AS SELECT id, notes FROM users;` ahead of the drop would preserve the contents — say the word and I'll add it.
